topic: General Business Law, Entity Licensing & Ethics
question: When a corporation, partnership, or association applies for a Pennsylvania broker's license, who must independently satisfy the broker qualification and application requirements of RELRA Sections 511-512?
choice_a: Every shareholder, partner, or member of the entity, regardless of role
choice_b: No individual needs to qualify; the entity's business registration alone suffices
choice_c: The individual designated as broker of record for that entity
choice_d: Only the entity's registered agent for service of process
explanation: RELRA Section 513 requires that, when a corporation, partnership, or association seeks a broker's license, the individual designated as broker of record must independently meet Sections 511 (qualifications) and 512 (application); other employees actually engaging in the real estate business must separately meet the salesperson requirements of Sections 521-522.
source_note: 63 P.S. Section 455.513 (confirmed verbatim, cross-referenced from this bank's Office Management bucket)

topic: General Business Law, Entity Licensing & Ethics
question: Under RELRA Section 604(4), which advertising practice is specifically disciplinable?
choice_a: Advertising a listing on more than one website simultaneously
choice_b: Advertising without including the licensee's photograph
choice_c: Advertising a property before the listing agreement is fully executed
choice_d: Any misleading or untruthful advertising, or using a trade name/insignia implying membership in a real estate association the licensee does not actually belong to
explanation: RELRA Section 604(4) makes it a disciplinable act to engage in misleading or untruthful advertising, or to use a trade name, insignia, or claimed membership in a real estate association/organization to which the licensee does not actually belong.

topic: General Business Law, Entity Licensing & Ethics
question: Under RELRA Section 604(19), is a licensee permitted to accept an undisclosed commission, rebate, or compensation from a party involved in a transaction?
choice_a: No -- paying, accepting, giving, or charging any undisclosed commission, rebate, compensation, or profit for a principal (or otherwise in violation of the act) is a disciplinable act
choice_b: Yes, as long as the amount is under $250
choice_c: Yes, without any disclosure requirement whatsoever
choice_d: Only sellers, not buyers, are protected from undisclosed compensation arrangements
explanation: Section 604(19) prohibits paying, accepting, giving, or charging any UNDISCLOSED commission, rebate, compensation, or profit connected to a principal's transaction -- reinforcing the broader RELRA theme (echoed in Section 606.1(a)(13)) that financial interests and compensation arrangements must be transparently disclosed to consumers.

topic: General Business Law, Entity Licensing & Ethics
question: Is a licensed auctioneer performing authorized auction duties at a bona fide auction required to also hold a real estate broker's license under RELRA?
choice_a: Yes -- every auctioneer selling real property must separately hold a PA broker's license
choice_b: No -- Section 304(9) exempts an auctioneer licensed under the Auctioneers' License Act while performing authorized duties at a bona fide auction
choice_c: Only auctioneers selling commercial (not residential) real estate are exempt
choice_d: The exemption applies only to online auctions, not in-person auctions
explanation: RELRA Section 304(9) exempts an auctioneer licensed under the act of September 29, 1961 (P.L.1745, No.708), the 'Auctioneers' License Act,' from RELRA's licensing requirement while performing authorized duties at a bona fide auction -- a targeted carve-out for a separately regulated profession.

topic: General Business Law, Entity Licensing & Ethics
question: Under the national broker content outline's Risk Management subtopic, which two types of insurance coverage are specifically listed as relevant to a broker's practice?
choice_b: Only title insurance, which brokers are required to personally carry
choice_c: Errors and Omissions (E&O) insurance and General Liability insurance
explanation: The national outline's Risk Management subtopic (Section IV.D.5-6, 'Types of insurance') lists Errors and Omissions (E&O) insurance and General Liability insurance as the specific coverages tested -- protecting brokers and agents against claims of professional negligence or general premises/operations liability, respectively.
source_note: Pearson VUE National/General Exam Content Outline for Brokers, effective April 1, 2025, Section IV.D.5-6 (confirmed directly from the official candidate handbook PDF)

topic: General Business Law, Entity Licensing & Ethics
question: Under the national broker content outline's Risk Management subtopic, what general category of federal law is tested alongside vicarious liability and fraud/misrepresentation?
explanation: The national outline's Section IV.D.4 lists 'Antitrust laws' as a tested Risk Management subtopic -- covering practices such as price-fixing among competing brokerages (e.g., agreeing on a uniform commission rate) and group boycotts, both of which can violate federal antitrust law (notably the Sherman Antitrust Act).
source_note: Pearson VUE National/General Exam Content Outline for Brokers, effective April 1, 2025, Section IV.D.4 (confirmed directly from the official candidate handbook PDF)

topic: General Business Law, Entity Licensing & Ethics
question: Would two competing Pennsylvania brokerages agreeing between themselves to charge an identical, fixed commission rate to all clients likely violate antitrust law?
choice_a: Yes -- this is a classic example of price-fixing among competitors, generally illegal under federal antitrust law (the Sherman Antitrust Act) regardless of state real estate licensing law
choice_b: No -- commission rates are set by the Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission, so an agreement merely reflects the mandated rate
choice_c: No -- antitrust law applies only to publicly traded companies, not real estate brokerages
choice_d: Yes, but only if the agreement is put in writing; an informal verbal understanding is permitted
explanation: This tests the national outline's antitrust subtopic directly: horizontal price-fixing agreements between competing brokerages -- whether written or merely understood informally -- are a per se violation of federal antitrust law, independent of the fact that RELRA itself (as covered in this bank's Commission bucket) does not set or cap commission rates.
source_note: Pearson VUE National/General Exam Content Outline for Brokers, effective April 1, 2025, Section IV.D.4 (confirmed general subject matter); Sherman Antitrust Act price-fixing doctrine is standard, well-corroborated national content, hedge: not independently pinpoint-cited to a specific case in this pass

topic: General Business Law, Entity Licensing & Ethics
question: Under the national broker content outline's Risk Management subtopic, what does 'vicarious liability' generally mean in the brokerage context?
choice_a: A form of liability that applies only to unlicensed employees, never licensees
choice_b: A broker's potential liability for the acts of an affiliated salesperson or associate broker performed within the scope of that affiliation
choice_c: A type of liability insurance policy, not a legal doctrine
choice_d: Liability that only attaches after a criminal conviction
explanation: Vicarious liability (Section IV.D.3 of the national outline) is the general legal principle that a principal (here, the broker) may be held liable for the acts of an agent (here, an affiliated salesperson or associate broker) performed within the scope of the agency relationship -- a concept that interacts with, but is legally distinct from, RELRA's own imputed-knowledge standard for LICENSE discipline under Section 702.
source_note: Pearson VUE National/General Exam Content Outline for Brokers, effective April 1, 2025, Section IV.D.3 (confirmed general subject matter); distinguished from 63 P.S. Section 455.702's narrower actual-knowledge standard for license discipline (confirmed verbatim, cross-referenced from this bank's License Law bucket)

topic: General Business Law, Entity Licensing & Ethics
question: How many hours of continuing education must a Pennsylvania broker or salesperson complete during each 2-year license period, under RELRA Section 404.1(b)?
explanation: RELRA Section 404.1(b) requires 14 hours of mandatory continuing education during each 2-year license period, matching the figure independently confirmed on the PA Real Estate Commission's own Broker Standard Licensure Snapshot page; the same 14-hour figure also applies to reactivating a license that has been placed on inactive status.

topic: General Business Law, Entity Licensing & Ethics
question: For how long may a Pennsylvania real estate license be placed on inactive status before the licensee must retake the appropriate examination to reactivate it?
choice_c: Inactive status has no time limit under RELRA
explanation: RELRA Section 404.1(e)(1),(4) requires renewal notices to inform licensees that a license may be placed on inactive status for no more than 5 years, and that a licensee who fails to reactivate within that window must retake the appropriate licensing examination -- simply documenting 14 hours of continuing education is no longer sufficient once the 5-year mark passes.

topic: General Business Law, Entity Licensing & Ethics
question: Under RELRA Section 404.1(c), when may a licensee receive continuing education credit for an office management course?
choice_a: Only when the course is offered to BROKERS and is intended to promote knowledge of the supervisory duties RELRA and Commission regulations impose on brokers (e.g., recordkeeping, escrow, advertising, conflicts of interest, disclosures)
choice_b: For any office management course, regardless of audience or content
choice_c: Office management courses never qualify for continuing education credit under any circumstance
choice_d: Only for courses taught exclusively online, never in person
explanation: Section 404.1(c) narrows office-management CE credit specifically to courses offered to BROKERS that promote knowledge of their supervisory duties under RELRA and Commission regulations -- covering document preparation/retention, recordkeeping, escrow account maintenance, advertising/solicitation limits, conflicts of interest, required disclosures, and general ethical responsibilities.

topic: General Business Law, Entity Licensing & Ethics
question: May the Commission waive all or part of a licensee's continuing education requirement?
choice_a: No -- the continuing education requirement can never be waived for any reason
choice_b: Yes -- the Commission may waive all or part of the requirement upon satisfactory evidence that the licensee was unable to complete it due to illness, emergency, or hardship
choice_c: Yes, but only for licensees over the age of 70
choice_d: Yes, automatically, for any licensee who requests it in writing
explanation: RELRA Section 404.1(a) gives the Commission discretion to waive all or part of the continuing education requirement upon satisfactory evidence that illness, emergency, or hardship prevented the licensee from completing it -- a meaningful, if discretionary, accommodation built into the CE framework.
